polarity.desc: corroborates the Pitiless→Chatterfang producer-choice witness with a second, independent any-color→specific-pip pair: Birds of Paradise's 'add one mana of any color' pays Horseshoe Crab's {U} (producer picks blue). Second witness, distinct producer/consumer/color — climbs the ladder.

match_policy.subject: cover
match_policy.desc: an argument-consume (a cost) demands the supplied object's at-creation type provably COVER the parameter filter (stricter than intersect)

match_policy.subject: cover
match_policy.desc: a counters STATE emit supplies a counter-removal cost (an argument-consume that spends counters as an activation cost, CR 602.1a/118.1) when the emitted counter-type COVERS the required removal type (+1/+1 covers +1/+1). Because a counter is NOT an object and has no characteristics (CR 122.1), this is a resource-supply match distinct from policy:argument:subject-cover (which covers an OBJECT's card-type). The counter must be placeable on the cost-payer: when the emit's target is producer-choice among you-controlled objects (target=chosen, control=you), the producer reliably lands the counter on the payer -> GREEN; a non-controllable / opponent-chosen target would only Overlap the payer (operator tiers AMBER). CR 122.6: counters put on an on-battlefield object are available to that object's abilities.

match_policy.subject: facet-feeds
match_policy.desc: a damage-dealt emit feeds a damage-dealt subscription only when the combat facets are compatible: a general trigger (combat=any, CR 120) fires on either combat or noncombat damage; a combat-specific trigger (CR 510) is fed ONLY by a combat emit; a noncombat emit NEVER feeds a combat-specific trigger. Directional on the combat axis (the manner-feeds constraint the combat-damage-modeling blocker named; engine CombatFacetFeeds).

match_policy.subject: facet-feeds
match_policy.desc: corroborates the soul-warden-x-ajanis-pridemate witness of policy:life-direction-match with (a) the FIRST loss-branch witness -- Sanguine Bond's opponent-loss emit feeds Exquisite Blood's opponent-loss subscription (loss feeds loss, edge E2), where soul-warden exercised only the gain branch -- and (b) a re-witness of the gain branch (Exquisite's you-gain emit feeds Sanguine's you-gain subscription, edge E4). Byte-identical core (consume_kind=subscription, subject=facet-feeds) and same axis/lattice/cr -> a reference, not a re-definition. Additionally the FIRST closed-CYCLE witness of the rule: soul-warden was one open pairwise feed, this pairs two direction-matched feeds into a self-sustaining life-mirror loop. The life 'mirror' needs NO new rule -- each card's gain<->loss FLIP is its own card-defined trigger->emit edge, so both cross-card edges are plain same-direction feeds under THIS rule.

match_policy.subject: trigger-subject-return
match_policy.desc: an external permanent's dies-trigger whose paid effect RETURNS the triggering creature to the battlefield: a returntobattlefield (recur, from=graveyard->to=battlefield) emit driven by a permanent OTHER than the returned card, keyed on that creature's death, that returns THAT card (the exact nontoken creature whose leaves-the-battlefield-to-graveyard event fired the trigger, CR 603.6e/603.10a) under the trigger-controller's control (CR 400.7 -- a new object put onto the battlefield by an effect). Because the returned object is the trigger's OWN captured subject (not a producer choice, not the driver's self-identity), the recast/return subject Subsumes on identity -> GREEN-eligible; but the return is performed by an EXTERNAL object (the reanimator, e.g. Nim Deathmantle the Equipment, NOT the returned creature itself) and it is a direct battlefield RETURN by an effect, NOT a CAST -- so it does NOT pay the returned creature's own mana cost, only the trigger's activation/pay co-cost (guard:recast-pays-mana; here Deathmantle's {4}, paid during resolution, CR 608.2). The EXTERNAL-AGENT dual of policy:recast:battlefield-return (self-return, where the returned object IS the driver card and casts ITSELF from the graveyard via a static permission, CR 601.3): there the agent and the returned object are ONE card; here they are DISTINCT cards -- a triggered reanimation of an external creature. Any loop closed by this reanimate still carries the pay co-cost, which floors the cycle to AMBER unless the loop provably refills that mana (Ashnod's {C}{C} covers only 2 of Deathmantle's {4} per single sac -> mana-negative -> AMBER; a token-doubling reanimation target refills it -> GREEN).

match_policy.subject: self-return
match_policy.desc: a returntobattlefield emit -- a permanent cast or reanimated from the graveyard directly ONTO the battlefield (from=graveyard, to=battlefield; e.g. a static 'you may cast this from your graveyard' permission, CR 601.3) -- refuels a self-recast when the returned object IS the recast subject (self:true). Because the card returns ITSELF (Gravecrawler's own death to the graveyard satisfies its own from=graveyard cast precondition), the recast subject Subsumes (not merely Overlaps) -> GREEN-eligible on identity; the battlefield-return analog of policy:recast:spell-recursion (which returns to HAND and Overlaps a target-chosen spell -> AMBER on identity). Any loop CLOSED by this recast still carries the recast's mana co-cost (guard:recast-pays-mana), which floors the cycle to AMBER unless the loop provably refills that cost in the RIGHT color.

match_policy.subject: self-return
match_policy.desc: a spell self-cast DIRECTLY from the graveyard via a static alternative-cost permission -- escape (CR 702.138a), flashback (CR 702.34a), or retrace (CR 702.81), each granting 'you may cast this card from your graveyard' (the casting permission of CR 601.3, paid as an alternative cost per 601.2b/601.2f-h) -- refuels the card's OWN cast:spell:self recast driver (subject=self-return, self:true) directly from the graveyard. The spell is cast onto the STACK, resolves, and is put into the graveyard (608.2n, escape/retrace) or exile (702.34a, flashback) -- it NEVER enters the battlefield. Because the card casts ITSELF, the recast subject Subsumes on identity -> GREEN-eligible, and guard:self-recast-samecard passes. The THIRD member of the recast family, distinct on the SOURCE ZONE + DESTINATION mechanism from both siblings: (1) policy:recast:spell-recursion returns the card to HAND first and re-casts a TARGET-chosen spell from hand (subject=intersect, Overlaps->AMBER, typically cross-card) -- THIS arm has no return-to-hand step and is self-return (Subsumes); (2) policy:recast:battlefield-return also casts from=graveyard and is self-return, but the object is a PERMANENT arriving ON the battlefield (to=battlefield, an ETB permanent, e.g. Gravecrawler) -- an escaped/flashed-back instant or sorcery resolves OFF the stack and is never a battlefield permanent, and escape additionally pays an exile-fuel co-cost (exile N other cards from your graveyard) that battlefield-return lacks. Two genuine axes of difference (destination stack vs battlefield; exile-fuel co-cost) -> a fresh declare, NOT a sibling of battlefield-return (reusing that id would collide, same-id/different-content) and NOT a from=graveyard attr on spell-recursion (different subject and no return-to-hand). Any loop closed by this recast carries the recast mana co-cost (guard:recast-pays-mana) and, for escape, the exile-fuel co-cost -- both floor the cycle to AMBER unless provably refilled.

match_policy.subject: intersect
match_policy.desc: a returntohand:permanent BOUNCE emit (from=battlefield -> to=hand, a permanent returned from the battlefield to its owner's hand) refuels the RECAST of the bounced permanent: recast from hand (CR 601.2, full mana repaid -> guard:recast-pays-mana), the permanent re-enters as a new object (CR 603.6e/400.7) and re-fires its self-ETB subscription. The PERMANENT dual of policy:recast:spell-recursion, distinct on three axes: (1) the returned object is a PERMANENT with an ETB, not an instant/sorcery SPELL with a cast trigger; (2) from=BATTLEFIELD (a bounce), not from=graveyard (graveyard recursion); (3) it terminates at the redeploy's self-ETB (a permanent's recast IS its re-entry), not at a cast:spell:self driver. Distinct from blink (deployment:creature[manner=blink], a DIRECT battlefield return, mana-free, no hand step) and from policy:recast:battlefield-return (a self-CAST from=graveyard directly ONTO the battlefield, CR 601.3). Feasible when the returned permanent's type Intersects the recast target; the operator tiers Subsumes->GREEN / Overlaps->AMBER -- a producer-choice return ('return ANOTHER permanent that shares a permanent type') Overlaps the specific creature the player wants to recast -> AMBER. Any loop closed by this bounce-recast carries the recast mana co-cost (guard:recast-pays-mana) and floors below GREEN unless the loop provably refills it in the right color (Priest of Gix's {B}{B}{B} refills {2}{B} -> mana parity, still AMBER via the producer-choice/'may' Overlap).

match_policy.subject: intersect
match_policy.desc: a cast:spell recast-driver consume (a spell watching to be re-cast, isSelf) is refueled by a returntohand:spell emit whose returned card lands in a castable zone (to=hand, CR 601.2); the match is feasible when the returned-object type Intersects the cast self-type, and the operator tiers the certainty Subsumes->GREEN / Overlaps->AMBER (a targeted 'return an instant or sorcery' is producer-choice -> Overlaps the specific recast spell -> AMBER). The recast/refuel-side analogue of policy:subscription:subject-intersect; implements the SpellRecursionSatisfiesCast arm's Intersects feasibility.

match_policy.subject: self-return
match_policy.desc: undying/persist death-driven SELF-recursion: a creature's OWN dies event (a removal:creature[self] put into the graveyard from the battlefield, CR 603.6 zone-change trigger) satisfies a returntobattlefield[self:true] recur emit that re-enters the SAME permanent onto the battlefield under its owner's control (undying CR 702.93a, persist CR 702.79) -- refueling its own death loop. A NEW recursion driver, sibling-but-DISTINCT from the two recast policies: (1) policy:recast:battlefield-return refuels a self-CAST from the graveyard (CR 601.3) that RE-PAYS full mana every iteration (guard:recast-pays-mana); (2) policy:recast:spell-recursion re-casts a spell from HAND (CR 601.2). Undying is a TRIGGERED-ABILITY return, NOT a cast: the permanent returns directly as the trigger resolves -- no stack-spell, no mana cost -> guard:recast-pays-mana DOES NOT apply and the loop is mana-free. Because the return is the SAME object (self:true), the recast subject Subsumes on identity (GREEN-eligible), UNLIKE blink's 'another creature' Overlaps floor (guard:self-watch). Any loop closed by this driver is instead gated by undying's counter-state condition (guard:undying-counter-reset), not a mana co-cost. Distinct on three axes -- trigger vs cast, no-mana vs full-mana-repayment, counter-parity vs mana-parity -- so a fresh declare, not a corroboration of either recast policy.

match_policy.subject: intersect
match_policy.desc: a subscription-consume (a trigger) matches on intersect; the operator tiers Subsumes→GREEN / Overlaps→AMBER

match_policy.subject: intersect
match_policy.desc: corroborates policy:subscription:subject-intersect (Deadeye) with the GREEN branch: when the emit subject provably Subsumes the subscription filter (creature ⊆ creature), the edge is GREEN

match_policy.subject: firing-multiplier
match_policy.desc: a trigger-firing MULTIPLIER intercept (an effect that makes a triggered ability trigger additional times, CR 603.2d — Teysa Karlov / Panharmonicon family) covers a triggered-ability SUBSCRIPTION and multiplies its firings when (a) the subscription's trigger-CAUSE event is covered by the multiplier's watched cause (Teysa: a creature dying, removal:creature[to=graveyard]; Blood Artist's cause creature ⊆ creature), and (b) the subscription's SOURCE permanent is covered by the multiplier's ability-owner control scope (Teysa: 'a permanent you control'; Blood Artist is a permanent you control). Distinct from the structural §4 modifier arm (grave-titan-x-anointed-procession, mechanism=modifier, self-certifying): that arm multiplies the MAGNITUDE of an EMIT event via single-referent stem-cover (the intercept watches the same event the emitter emits); THIS policy multiplies the FIRINGS of a SUBSCRIPTION (a consume-side triggered ability) and requires a DUAL-referent match (trigger-cause cover AND ability-owner control cover) that structural emit-cover cannot certify. Ceiling GREEN: the multiplication is mandatory and deterministic (603.2d, no 'may'), reliability-bounded only by the shared premise that both the source permanent and the multiplier are under your control. No loop: 603.2d — 'an effect that states that an ability triggers additional times doesn't invoke itself repeatedly'; the extra trigger is a one-shot per-death magnitude multiplier, not a repeating cycle.

guards.desc: the another-object / exclude=self identity guard: a self-excluding consume must not match the same object (Pitiless watches ANOTHER creature)

an additional-combat driver (an emit on combat-presence, control=you — 'there is an additional combat phase', CR 500.8) that satisfies a creature's re-attack subscription (combat-presence, subject=self) can NEVER certify GREEN, even though control=you covers subject=self: re-attacking is a CHOICE (CR 508.1a 'if any' — attackers are declared, never forced), the attacker may be blocked, and the combat-damage it re-drives is Gated (once per combat, CR 510). So any loop through the extra-combat re-attack floors to AMBER — the §8 soundness floor for the extra-combat arm, mirroring how the Gated combat-damage emit prevents a false GREEN

a recast emit (emit:cast - a spell bounced/returned to a castable zone and cast again, CR 601) re-pays the spell's full mana cost every iteration. A cast-loop that is closed BY a recast therefore carries an irreducible mana co-cost: the loop is sound (GREEN-eligible) only if it provably refills that cost; unrefilled - or refilled only through an AMBER mana bridge (untap->mana) - the loop floors to AMBER (ADR-0003 §8 mana balance). Caps the cast->cast-trigger edge that the recast closes.

the SpellRecursionSatisfiesCast same-card self-recast prune: a card whose return-to-hand returns OTHER cards (emit subject not self) can NEVER satisfy its OWN cast:spell:self driver — a spell is cast from where it is (CR 601.2), and an other-card / exile return is not THIS spell in hand (Pair o' Dice Lost returns other graveyard cards and exiles itself, so it is not its own recast subject). Prunes the spurious 1-card self-loop; the CROSS-card recursion (Archaeomancer returns Ghostly Flicker) is a different card and unaffected. The recast dual of guard:self-watch (both same-card object-identity guards, CR 400.7).
a self-watching trigger (subject=self) requires a same-card witness that the emitted object IS the watcher; object identity the operator can't see → Overlaps floors AMBER

the undying/persist counter-parity loop-soundness floor (the counter analogue of guard:recast-pays-mana's mana-parity): undying returns the creature ONLY 'if it had no +1/+1 counters on it' and puts it back 'with a +1/+1 counter on it' (CR 702.93a / 122.1). A self-recursion loop closed by policy:recur:death-return-self is therefore re-armable ONLY if each iteration REMOVES that returned +1/+1 counter before the creature next dies -- otherwise the second death has a +1/+1 counter on it, undying's condition fails, and the loop halts after a single return. Caps policy:recur:death-return-self: GREEN-eligible only when the loop provably resets the +1/+1 counter to zero every cycle (here Walking Ballista's 'Remove a +1/+1 counter' cost spends exactly the returned counter; net counter change per iteration = 0). Persist is the dual with -1/-1 counters (return only if none, come back with one). The state the loop must reset to stay sound, the counter-parity sibling of the recast mana-parity guard.

the self-untap's activation cost places a cumulative -1/-1 counter on the source (CR 118.1 cost / 122.1 counter), permanently weakening it each renewal; a creature reaching toughness 0 or less is put into its graveyard as a state-based action (CR 704.5f). So a self-untap loop closed by this counter cost carries an irreducible -1/-1 'toughness-budget' co-cost -- BOUNDED by the source's starting toughness on its own, no closed infinite cycle. The loop is GREEN-eligible (truly infinite) only when an external effect refills that budget: a -1/-1 counter remover/preventer (Vizier of Remedies replaces the -1/-1 with zero counters) or a noncreature-type change (Swift Reconfiguration -- 704.5f then no longer applies). The counter analogue of guard:recast-pays-mana (a mana co-cost that floors a loop unless the resource is provably refilled) -- the section-8/SDF co-cost cap for the self-untap-via-counter arm.

bridges.desc: a copy's inherited BLINK emit (deployment:creature[manner=blink]) that blinks the tap-gated COPIER renews the copier's tap:self cost: the copier re-enters the battlefield as a new UNTAPPED object (CR 603.6e/400.7), so its {T} ability is available again. The blink-arm dual of the inherited-untap closing hop (copy-inheritance-scope.md Decision 4; engine BlinkReachesSource + the blink branch of GraftCopyInheritance's closing hops). Ceiling AMBER, never GREEN: the ETB carrying the blink is Gated ('you may', CR 603.6e -- the optional ETB cannot be certified to fire), and the 'another target creature you control' clause only Overlaps the specific copier (object identity the operator cannot see -- guard:self-watch). A soundness-preserving floor even when the loop is mana-free and summoning-sickness-free (the copier's own haste clears the sickness gate). Distinct from bridge:spell-copy-to-cast-driver (a STACK spell-copy that re-fires a cast driver and never enters the battlefield) and from bridge:untap-land-to-mana (untap->mana): this is a battlefield permanent-copy's blink renewing a tap cost.

a damage-dealt emit feeds a dies event (removal:creature[to=graveyard]) when the marked damage is lethal: total damage marked on a creature >= its toughness -> the creature is destroyed as a state-based action (CR 120.6 / 302.7 -> 704), i.e. it is put into the graveyard from the battlefield and dies. Supplies the damage->death transition the parser proves only as a damage emit (the event_verbs note 'damage-dealt ... when lethal, removal (state-based death)'). Ceiling AMBER, never GREEN: lethality is BOARD-STATE-dependent -- it holds only when marked damage provably >= toughness, which the operator cannot see in general (a ping is usually non-lethal), and it is reliability-capped by damage prevention / regeneration / indestructible / toughness-boost replacements. Contrast bridge:sacrifice-to-dies (GREEN, a deterministic rules zone-change independent of board state): a sacrifice always dies; damage dies only if lethal. Distinct from the cross-resource untap->mana / copy->cast bridges.

a damage-dealt emit whose source has lifelink causes that source's controller to gain that much life (CR 702.15b, which references 120.3), and that life-gain feeds a 'whenever you gain life' subscription (CR 119.9; the gain->gain direction match is policy:life-direction-match, reused). The damage->life resource crossing. Ceiling AMBER, never GREEN: lifelink is a static keyword the operator often cannot prove is present - most sharply when it is GRANTED (Heliod's '{1}{W}: another target creature gains lifelink') and the parser projects the grant only as coarse emit:gainability (keyword=lifelink not AST-derivable) - so whether a given damage emit yields life is unprovable. The granted-keyword (lifelink) parse is the PARSER TARGET, mirroring bridge:untap-land-to-mana's cross-resource AMBER and deadeye's blink-as-gainability. A damage emit from a NON-lifelink source yields no life at all (CR 120.3) - the reason this can never be a blanket GREEN.

a sacrifice (removal:creature[manner=sacrificed] emit) feeds a dies-trigger (removal:creature[to=graveyard] subscription): CR 701.21a — to sacrifice a permanent is to move it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard — so it dies (CR 700.4, leaves-the-battlefield to graveyard). The bridge supplies the to=graveyard destination the parser proves only as manner=sacrificed (the ADR-2 sac-consume → ltb:…:to-graveyard-consume arm, PortGraphEngine.AddCoarseRulesEdges (3)). Ceiling GREEN — a deterministic rules zone-change (contrast the AMBER cross-resource untap→mana / copy→cast bridges): the edge is GREEN when the sacrificed type provably covers the dies-watch filter, reliability-capped only by a graveyard-replacement (Rest in Peace) board prune.

a STACK spell-copy (emit:copy:spell, CR 707.10 -- the copy is put on the stack and is NOT cast) reproduces the copied spell's OWN effects, re-firing a type-compatible spell's cast:spell:self effect-DRIVER (never a cast trigger). Irreducible ceiling AMBER: the copied 'instant or sorcery' filter only Intersects the driver's IsSelf self-type (the IsSelf Subsumes=No floor). NOTE: from_attrs.resource=spell is the load-bearing variant discriminator (only a spell-copy, not a permanent token-copy, re-fires a cast driver) but resource is NOT yet a licensed attribute_axis -- surfaced as an axis decision, not an authored port attr.

untapping a CREATURE renews a creature-tap-for-mana ability - an EXTERNAL activated ability ('tap an untapped [blue] creature you control: add mana', e.g. Grand Architect) that taps the creature for mana. The creature dual of bridge:untap-land-to-mana, but a genuinely different arm: the land bridge's untapped permanent self-taps for mana (one object, intrinsic mana source), whereas here the untapped creature is NOT a mana source - a separate ability taps it (two objects). So the inference is 'untap creature -> external tap-for-mana can re-fire -> mana', not 'untap land -> land taps itself'. Irreducible cross-resource (untap != mana, CR 107.4); AMBER ceiling because the external tap-for-mana ability chooses 'AN untapped creature you control' (producer choice / object identity the operator cannot see, CR 400.7) and the produced mana may carry a spend-restriction. Distinct from bridge:blink-renews-tap (a blink re-entry that renews a tap COST, to_stem=tap) - this renews the untapped STATE that gates the mana.
untapping lands enables (does not produce) mana; irreducible cross-resource — untapped lands' colors/count are unknown

an untap (structure:untap emit) renews a tap-based cost/ability (tap consume): the untapped permanent's {T} activated ability or tap-cost becomes available again (CR 701.26 untap keyword action; CR 107.5 the {T} cost; CR 602 re-activation). Ceiling GREEN -- a mandatory, universal untap reliably renews the tap (witnessed by Intruder Alarm's 'untap all creatures'); individual edges floor to AMBER via their own residual guards: object-identity Overlap on a targeted untap (guard:self-watch) or a cumulative counter co-cost (guard:untap-cost-accrues-counter). Collapses the batch-9 per-outlet siblings (ETB-targeted / universal-creature / self-via-counter) into one relation -- the differences are the untap's trigger/target (far side of the emit), not the untap->tap bridge.
